title: Shantideva: Working with Anger
speaker: Nomon Tim Burnett
summary: Nomon Tim Burnett takes up Shantideva's chapter 5, "The Guarding of Awareness," and his chapter 6 on patience (kshanti), reading the verses that tell an arrogant or irritated mind to remain like a block of wood. Nomon tests the teaching on anger against the previous day, when a nationwide grounding of flights stranded travelers and indignation at Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy rose in Nomon's own mind. Shantideva's answers include conditioning, shared delusion, and the child wailing over a broken sandcastle, until the chapter arrives at longing for an enemy like a treasure found at home. Nomon closes with tomorrow's Shosan and precepts ceremonies, in which Katie and Trish receive new Buddhist names.

*Whenever one wishes to move or to speak, first one should examine one's own mind and then act appropriately and with self-possession.

*When, seeming to advance yourself, you are actually deprecating others, contemptuous and scornful, one should definitely remain like a block of wood.*

*When I see my mind is seeking acquisition, reverence or renown, trying to look good, and wants an audience and attention, I remember I should remain like a block of wood.
When my mind is foul-tempered, intolerant, idle, cowardly, biased in my own favor, I should remain like a block of wood.*
It's very thorough.
*Noticing in this way that the mind is defiled or engaged in fruitless activity, the wise one should always firmly curb it with the antidote to that condition.
I shall instead be determined, full of serene confidence, steady, full of appreciation and respect.

Block of wood.
